q: Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called ______.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called semiconductors. Conductors or insulators is not this quantity.

q: In semiconductors, the charge carriers are ______.
e: In a semiconductor both electrons and positive holes carry charge. In semiconductors, the charge carriers are electrons and positive holes. Only electrons or only positive holes is not this quantity.

q: A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a ______.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a positive hole. Do not trade positive hole for free electron or valence gap.

q: Pure semiconductors have poor conductivity at normal temperature because ______.
a: the number of electrons and holes is relatively few
they are made of non-metallic elements
e: A pure semiconductor has few electrons and holes at room temperature, so it conducts poorly. Pure semiconductors have poor conductivity at normal temperature because the number of electrons and holes is relatively few. They contain no charge carriers or they are made of non-metallic elements is not this quantity.

q: When arsenic atoms are added to pure germanium or silicon, the resulting semiconductor is called ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When arsenic atoms are added to pure germanium or silicon, the resulting semiconductor is called n-type semiconductor. P-type semiconductor or compound semiconductor is not this quantity.

q: In an n-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are ______.
e: In a semiconductor both electrons and positive holes carry charge. In an n-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are electrons. Positive holes or protons is not this quantity.

q: When indium atoms are added to pure silicon or germanium, the resulting semiconductor is called ______.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. When indium atoms are added to pure silicon or germanium, the resulting semiconductor is called p-type semiconductor. N-type semiconductor or intrinsic semiconductor is not this quantity.

q: In a p-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are ______.
e: In a semiconductor both electrons and positive holes carry charge. In a p-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are positive holes. Electrons or neutrons is not this quantity.

q: Germanium and silicon are examples of ______.
e: Germanium and silicon are examples of elemental semiconductors. Compound semiconductors or insulators is not this quantity.

q: Gallium arsenide (GaAs) is an example of a ______.
e: Ge and Si are elemental semiconductors. GaAs and CdTe are compound semiconductors. Gallium arsenide (GaAs) is an example of a compound semiconductor. Metallic conductor or pure insulator is not this quantity.

q: The process of adding impurity atoms to a pure semiconductor to increase its conductivity is called ______.
e: A little donor or acceptor impurity, doping, makes n-type or p-type material and raises conductivity. The process of adding impurity atoms to a pure semiconductor to increase its conductivity is called doping. Do not trade doping for ionization or excitation.

q: A boundary formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors is called a ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. A boundary formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors is called a p-n junction. Depletion layer or bias region is not this quantity.

q: A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a ______.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a p-n junction diode. Transistor or rectifier is not this quantity.

q: When the positive terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the negative to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When the positive terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the negative to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be forward-biased. Do not trade forward-biased for reverse-biased or unbiased.

q: When the negative terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the positive to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When the negative terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the positive to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be reverse-biased. Forward-biased or neutral is not this quantity.

q: In a forward-biased p-n junction diode, ______.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. In a forward-biased p-n junction diode, a large current flows. No current flows or only minority carriers flow is not this quantity.

q: In a reverse-biased p-n junction diode, ______.
a: only a very small reverse current flows
current flows equally in both directions
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. In a reverse-biased p-n junction diode, only a very small reverse current flows. A large current flows or current flows equally in both directions is not this quantity.

q: Anode and cathode of an unconnected p-n junction are not at the same electric potential because ______.
a: there is initially a potential difference across the junction
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Anode and cathode of an unconnected p-n junction are not at the same electric potential because there is initially a potential difference across the junction. Do not trade there is initially a potential difference across the junction for external voltage is applied or the materials are different.

q: A rectifier is a device which converts ______.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. A rectifier is a device which converts AC to unidirectional current (DC). Do not trade AC to unidirectional current (DC) for DC to AC or high voltage to low voltage.

q: Diodes can be used as rectifiers because ______.
a: current flows in one direction only
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. Diodes can be used as rectifiers because current flows in one direction only. Do not trade current flows in one direction only for they amplify signals or they store electric charge.

q: A half-wave rectifier uses ______ diode(s).
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A half-wave rectifier uses one diode(s). Do not trade one for two or four.

q: A full-wave rectifier uses ______ diode(s).
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A full-wave rectifier uses two diode(s). Do not trade two for one or three.

q: In a half-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during ______.
a: both halves of the AC cycle
only the first half of the AC cycle
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. In a half-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during only the first half of the AC cycle. Do not trade only the first half of the AC cycle for both halves of the AC cycle or only when voltage is zero.

q: In a full-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during ______.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. In a full-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during both half-cycles. Do not trade both half-cycles for only the positive half-cycle or only the negative half-cycle.

q: Rectifiers are used in the power supply units of devices such as ______.
a: radio, television, and mobile phone chargers
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. Rectifiers are used in the power supply units of devices such as radio, television, and mobile phone chargers. Do not trade radio, television, and mobile phone chargers for electric heaters or incandescent bulbs.
